sca_fisher.text: Scalloway has the fish market, and the fish market has the fishermen, and the fishermen have all the opinions. I will not tell you which ones are right.
Mòran taing, they say in the west. Here we say 'tank you'. It is the same, only more windy.

sca_bus.text: The Shetland Bus is a proper story. Small boats, long nights, men who could have stayed at home. My grandfather said nothing about it. I am told that was the point.
Ask at the museum if you want the proper telling. I only know the bit I have been allowed to.

sca_castle.text: Patrick Stewart built this castle with forced labour and a lot of timber. He did not get to enjoy it for long. History is not always kind to men with a good eye for a view.
It was the capital of Shetland until 1708. After that, Lerwick took over, and Scalloway has been getting its own back ever since, mostly at the fish market.

sca_pony.text: Shetland ponies are small, hardy and thoroughly aware of both. Do not try to tell one what to do. Offer an apple and ask nicely.
They were bred to carry peat and children. They are very good at the first and have strong views on the second.

sca_foal.text: A small, very round pony trots up, takes in your pockets, and walks off with its dignity intact.
